name: The Nation cryptic crossword No 3274
preamble: Joshua Kosman and Henri Picciotto Share Copy Link Facebook X (Twitter) Bluesky Pocket Email March 5, 2013 This article appears in the March 25, 2013 issue.

clue.text: Timepiece starting late — it requires a key

indicators.note: a word that starts late has lost its opening letter, as if it began a beat after the rest

blocks.note: a timepiece on the wall or mantel

explanation.surface: A clock that runs late needs winding, and an old-fashioned one is wound with a key.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface ties the key to winding the clock; the definition is the beheaded word itself, which a key opens.
explanation.definitionFit: A lock is the fastening that only opens when the matching key is turned in it.

clue.text: Single payment broken down, plus… um… 1000?

indicators.note: broken down means taken apart, so the letters are reassembled differently

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Someone hesitantly working out a one-off payment, itemised, plus, um, a thousand?
explanation.definitionFit: A lump sum is money paid all at once instead of in instalments.

clue.text: Core group's California dreams, half-forgotten

indicators.note: if half is forgotten, only the first half of the word survives

blocks.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California
only its first half is kept

explanation.surface: A band's California dreams, half of them now forgotten, like faded hippie ideals.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadre is a small nucleus of trained or committed people around which a larger organisation is built.

clue.text: There are seven narcs involving sly criminal in rackets

indicators.note: the narcs are joined up with what follows, the two parts running on one after another
something criminal is bent or crooked, so the word before it is rearranged
one part is placed inside the other, sitting within it

blocks.note: the US Drug Enforcement Administration, whose agents are narcs
rackets meaning loud noises
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A report that seven drug agents were caught up with a cunning crook in protection rackets.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a riddle: the answer is the thing of which there are famously seven. Narcs is American slang for drug agents, and the DEA is their agency.
explanation.definitionFit: Christian tradition counts exactly seven deadly sins, pride, greed, lust, envy, gluttony, wrath and sloth, so 'there are seven' describes them.

clue.text: Beasts seen in Ethiopia and Eritrea?

definitions.note: read as E-LANDS, countries beginning with E

blocks.note: first meaning: large African antelopes
second meaning, a pun: two lands whose names start with E

explanation.surface: A wildlife question about which animals live in the Horn of Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as E + LANDS: both countries are lands beginning with E. The question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Elands are the large spiral-horned antelopes of the African savannah, so they are beasts.

clue.text: For the most part, pack coal in a winter month

indicators.note: most but not all of the word is kept, its last letter dropped

blocks.note: a pack of cards is a deck
an ember is a glowing coal

explanation.surface: Mostly, you stock up on coal for the cold months.
explanation.definitionFit: December falls in the northern winter, the last month of the year.

clue.text: You and two gods protect box for teenage musicians…

indicators.note: to protect something is to surround and shield it, so the gods go around it

blocks.note: taken as written
Thor, the Norse thunder god, and Ra, the Egyptian sun god
a chest is a large box

explanation.surface: Divine guardians watching over the instrument case of a band of young players, continuing into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The two gods split around the box, Thor before it and Ra after.
explanation.definitionFit: A youth orchestra is a full orchestra whose players are school-age, often teenagers.

clue.text: …in baroque concert, like this clue?

indicators.note: baroque means ornate and convoluted, so the words are twisted into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
the printed word has an N where the anagram needs a second R, a deliberate flaw

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: young players performing in a baroque concert.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearranging IN CONCERT gives two Ns and one R, while the answer needs one N and two Rs. The near-miss is the joke: a mistaken clue whose answer is the word for mistaken.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue's own wordplay is faulty, so calling the clue wrong or mistaken is accurate.

clue.text: A snake is a lousy present

indicators.note: lousy means poor or shoddy, so the word is badly put together in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Getting a snake as a gift would be a terrible present.
explanation.definitionFit: A serpent is a literary word for a snake, a long legless reptile.

clue.text: Choice directed the woman's call for something to eat — that's fishy

blocks.note: your pick is your choice
led means directed
her is the possessive for a woman
to ring someone is to call them on the phone

explanation.surface: Someone choosing who gets to phone for food, and smelling something suspicious about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's fishy' sounds like suspicion; here it is literal, the food is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickled herring is a preserved fish dish, eaten across Northern Europe and in Jewish delis.

clue.text: Wine created by Gershwin

blocks.note: made means created
Ira Gershwin, the lyricist brother of George

explanation.surface: Reads like a question about a vintage that the Gershwin brothers produced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gershwin' points first at George, but the letters come from his brother Ira, who wrote the lyrics.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeira is a fortified wine from the Portuguese island of the same name.

clue.text: Component of a train is iron, perhaps? About right

blocks.note: an iron is one kind of golf club
ca. is the abbreviation of circa, about
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether part of a locomotive is made of iron, and being told that's about right.
explanation.walkthrough: The railway surface makes iron sound like the metal; here it is the golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A club car is a railway carriage with a lounge or bar, one of the cars that make up a passenger train.

clue.text: Deviously hid smoke, consuming a piece of hashish in Arab territory

indicators.note: only a small piece is taken, the opening letter of the next word
consuming means taking something inside, so one letter goes within the other words
acting deviously means by a crooked route, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the first letter of hashish

explanation.surface: Someone secretly smoking a bit of hashish somewhere in the Arab world.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheikhdom is a land ruled by a sheikh, such as the Gulf states, so it is an Arab territory.

clue.text: Garden tool entails R&D for many people

indicators.note: to entail something is to include it, so the tool holds the other letters inside

blocks.note: a hoe is a long-handled weeding tool
R&D, research and development, with the ampersand dropped

explanation.surface: A company's new gardening implement requiring research and development on behalf of the many.
explanation.walkthrough: R&D is read as just its two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A horde is a large crowd or throng, so it describes many people.

clue.text: Grievous harm besets the French composer

indicators.note: grievous suggests something badly hurt, so the word after it is damaged into a new order
to beset is to surround on all sides, so one part closes round the other

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
le is a French word for the

explanation.surface: Serious injury befalls a French composer, like a tragic biography.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grievous harm' reads as one legal phrase, but grievous is the anagram signal; 'the French composer' wants to be one person, though 'the French' is LE and the definition is just composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Mahler was the Austrian late-Romantic composer of ten symphonies.

clue.text: Historian's sub-point on our gang

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the first parts sit atop the last

blocks.note: a hero is an American name for a submarine sandwich
a dot is a point
us is the group that includes we who are speaking

explanation.surface: A historian's subsidiary argument about the group we belong to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sub-point' reads as a minor point, but sub is the sandwich, which Americans also call a hero or hoagie.
explanation.definitionFit: Herodotus, the ancient Greek writer of the Histories, is called the father of history.

clue.text: Superlatively strange wild ride, in a certain direction

indicators.note: something wild is out of control, so the letters run loose into a new order
in places the scrambled letters inside the other part

blocks.note: west is one compass direction
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A rollercoaster heading off one way that is the oddest thing anyone has seen.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is spelled out as 'superlatively strange' to show the answer is a superlative adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Weirdest is the superlative of weird, so it means strangest of all.

clue.text: Gravity reshaped our ball to be round

indicators.note: something reshaped is given a new form, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: g is the physics symbol for acceleration due to gravity
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A physics remark: gravity pulls our planet into a sphere.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is real science: gravity is why planets are round.
explanation.definitionFit: Globular means shaped like a globe, so it is round in the spherical sense.

clue.text: Avoiding the opening, smash North Pole window

indicators.note: avoiding the opening means skipping the first letter of the words that follow
smashing something breaks it to pieces, so the remaining letters are reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An Arctic explorer breaking a window at the Pole while steering clear of the gap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' and 'window' look like they belong together, but 'the opening' is simply the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A porthole is the small round window in the side of a ship or aircraft.

clue.text: Beginning of Philippians' fertile lesson

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the first letter of Philippians
arable land is fertile, fit for crops

explanation.surface: Opening a sermon on a fruitful teaching from Paul's Letter to the Philippians.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bible surface fits the answer, as Jesus taught in such stories.
explanation.definitionFit: A parable is a short story told to teach a moral or spiritual lesson.

clue.text: Slides and photographs as part of a lecture

indicators.note: a lecture is spoken, so the word is to be heard rather than read

blocks.note: a photographer shoots pictures, so photographs means shoots

explanation.surface: A lecturer illustrating a talk with a slideshow and photos.
explanation.walkthrough: In a lecture, slides are projected pictures; here they are the things you slide down.
explanation.definitionFit: Chutes are sloping channels or playground slides down which people or things slide.

clue.text: Financial institution covers overtime where baseball might be played

indicators.note: in a down clue, covering means sitting on top, so the first part comes above the second

blocks.note: S&L, a savings and loan association, a US bank, with the ampersand read as AND
OT is the abbreviation for overtime

explanation.surface: A bank picking up the cost of extra hours at a ballpark.
explanation.walkthrough: A savings and loan is an American thrift bank, abbreviated S&L.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandlot is a vacant lot where children play informal games, especially baseball.

clue.text: It's, like, in New Hampshire, near the edges of USA!

definitions.text: It's, like, in New Hampshire, near the edges of USA!

indicators.note: in places one piece within the state's two-letter code
near means placed next to, so the last part follows on
the edges of a word are its outermost letters

blocks.note: NH is the postal abbreviation for New Hampshire
as and like both mean in the manner of
the outer letters of USA

explanation.surface: A breathless, slangy description of somewhere up in New Hampshire, by the country's borders.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: the city lies in New Hampshire, close to the state line.
explanation.definitionFit: Nashua is the second-largest city in New Hampshire, near the Massachusetts border.

clue.text: One way to identify speeding drivers: camera/darkroom contents

definitions.text: One way to identify speeding drivers

indicators.note: the contents of something are what is inside it, so the letters lie within the words

blocks.note: running across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Speed-trap photography: the camera and what is developed in the darkroom.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points at speed cameras, but the device that clocks a car's speed is the gun hidden here.
explanation.definitionFit: Police radar guns measure a vehicle's speed by bouncing radio waves off it, catching speeders.

clue.text: Bishop was into a dissolute naval officer

indicators.note: dissolute means loose-living, and loose letters may be reordered

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A churchman who was keen on a debauched sailor, a scandal headline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was into' reads as 'fancied', but all three words are letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A boatswain, or bosun, is the ship's officer in charge of rigging, anchors and the deck crew.

clue.text: Attach very loudly in Provençal city

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the name of the city

blocks.note: Aix-en-Provence, the city in southern France
ff, fortissimo, is the musical mark for very loud

explanation.surface: Someone loudly fastening something in a French town.
explanation.definitionFit: To affix is to fasten or stick one thing to another, so it means attach.

clue.text: Crime fighter and soldier interrupting spoiled brat at first hint of lawbreaking

indicators.note: something spoiled is ruined or messed up, so those letters are jumbled
to interrupt is to break in, so one piece is placed inside the other
the first hint of a word is just its opening letter
at here means placed next to, so the last letter follows on

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
GI is an American soldier
the first letter of lawbreaking

explanation.surface: A policeman and a soldier stepping in on a spoiled child the moment it starts misbehaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Batgirl is the masked comic-book heroine who fights crime in Gotham City alongside Batman.

clue.text: A bit of hemlock (as much as you can carry) is bad for you

indicators.note: a bit is a small piece, here only the first letter of the next word

blocks.note: the first letter of hemlock

blocks.clueFragment: as much as you can carry
blocks.note: an armful is as much as your arms can hold

explanation.surface: A little hemlock is poisonous, never mind an armload of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Hemlock is a famous poison, so the surface warning is accurate.
explanation.definitionFit: Something harmful does damage, so it is bad for you.

clue.text: "Great" means "engaged in the struggle," for a former Communist

indicators.note: words caught up in a struggle are tossed about and come out in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A Cold War comrade explaining that greatness means fighting the class struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make it look like a dictionary entry, but they simply wrap the letters to be shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: An East German was a citizen of the communist German Democratic Republic, which ceased to exist in 1990.

clue.text: Be without stamina, initially, and leave

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter is used
without means lacking, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: to be is to exist
the first letter of stamina

explanation.surface: Advice to someone running out of energy: just give up and go.
explanation.definitionFit: To exit is to go out of a place, so it is a synonym of leave as a verb.
